explanations: No defect. Deliveries are enqueued only after the event commits and are deduplicated per (endpoint, event); each attempt uses connect and read timeouts, a signed body, and a stable Webhook-Id. Responses are classified: 2xx delivered, 410 disables the endpoint, 408/429/5xx and network errors raise to let Sidekiq retry with jittered exponential backoff, and other 4xx fail permanently. Exhausted retries mark the delivery failed.
404 matches neither 2xx, 410, nor the retryable list, so the else branch records a permanent failure. Only 408, 429, 5xx and network errors raise RetryableError, and only 410 disables the endpoint.

Webhook-Id is delivery.event_id, stable across retries. The signature header contains a timestamp that is regenerated on every attempt, so it differs between retries, and the sender explicitly retries failures (at-least-once).

Enqueuing inside the transaction creates a race with the worker, which may look up a delivery that is not yet visible, and would fire for events that later roll back. after_commit runs once the data is durable. The unique constraint and timeouts are independent of the callback.
